target_customer: Underserved Mexican car owners, including rideshare drivers, who lack affordable auto insurance
problem: Mexico has tens of millions of uninsured vehicles because underwriting models are outdated and payment terms suit only affluent buyers. Momento became a licensed carrier to underwrite risk and price digitally.
business_model: Licensed auto insurance carrier selling policies through a mobile app and brokers, with monthly payments from 249 MXN

founders.name: Lois Rogel Vence
education: ICADE, Universidad Pontificia de Comillas, Law and Business Administration
founders.background_notes: Served financial institutions and private equity in Europe and the US per the YC page.

founders.name: Leon Bartolome Carreno
prior_employers: McKinsey and Company (Associate, 3 years, insurance strategy)
education: Imperial College London, Master's in Mechanical Engineering

competitors.name: Crabi
competitors.what: Mexican insurtech selling auto insurance digitally
competitors.funding_then: 4 million USD round led by Kaszek in October 2021

competitors.name: Guros
competitors.what: Online auto insurance marketplace in Mexico
competitors.funding_then: 5.8 million USD raised in 2021 per a trade article

technical_complexity.rationale: Pricing models, a mobile app for quoting and claims, and regulatory capital and reporting for a full carrier are demanding, but standard insurtech engineering.

defensibility.rationale: A CNSF carrier license, reinsurance relationships and underwriting data are hard to replicate quickly. Licensing took longer than the summer 2022 target, which shows the barrier.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Incumbents held 70 percent or more of the market per Bloomberg Linea in 2023 and did not acquire Momento. The company says it is CNSF approved and sells in 12 states.

market_need_then: The launch post cites over 30 million uninsured vehicles in Mexico and a 13 billion dollar untapped opportunity, with antiquated underwriting and payment terms for the affluent as pain points. Figures are the company's own.

branding.domain_note: Uses tumomento.com (a prefix on the real word, Spanish for your Momento) rather than momento.com; acquisition details not found.

identity.voice_and_tone: Innovative, transparent and fair; tagline El seguro de auto que lo cambia todo

branding.brand_signature: Tagline El seguro de auto que lo cambia todo and a 4.9 rated app
branding.community_and_virality: Company site lists press from Bloomberg Linea, WIRED, GQ and Reforma and over 4,700 Google reviews, self reported.

brand_strength.rationale: Some press and app ratings per the company site, but the name Momento is generic and shared with other companies, such as a serverless caching company. No independent brand coverage was found.

outcome_analysis: Momento took roughly a year longer than its stated summer 2022 target to obtain a carrier license, then launched in August 2023 with a 10.5 million USD seed and raised a 10 million Series A in August 2025 with more than 10,000 active customers claimed. It is active, regulated by the CNSF and rated by AM Best, so it is a slow but advancing regulated business.
notes: Seed confirmed by Bloomberg Linea (2023-08-04), The Insurer and Gunderson Dettmer. Series A: Gunderson says 10 million (2025-08-28) while Contxto reports 10.25 million (dated 2025-09-19) and Axios reported it earlier; the 10 million figure is used. Pre-2023 funding (YC standard deal and others) was not found; CB Insights total of 21.25 million over four rounds and a January 2026 Series A close date are unverified. The AM Best rating a+.MX (April 2026) comes from a search summary. Competitors Crabi and Guros are sourced to pre-batch articles; Crabi 4M round reported by Bloomberg Linea per its headline. Later rival Justos (Brazil) is not included because its source dates from 2023.
